#### **B. Measured Move Projections:**
The core technique taught is:

> **"When price forms a peak and then pulls back to a trough (dip), measure that distance (peak-to-trough). Project that same distance upward from the peak to estimate the next price target/key level."**

This creates upside **price targets** that serve as key resistance/profit-taking levels. The chart shows this methodology applied **multiple times** throughout the bull cycle, with each successive measured move projection being reached and often exceeded.

## 1. WHAT IS SHOWN

This is a **daily candlestick chart (D1)** of **SPY (S&P 500 ETF)** spanning approximately **mid-November through early April** (likely 2024-2025 based on the publication date of 2025-01-03). The chart uses a **hollow/filled candlestick** style where:

- **Green/hollow candles** = bullish (close above open)
- **Red/filled candles** = bearish (close below open)

A **volume histogram** is displayed at the bottom with a 10-period volume moving average (10VOL(10) = -4710652). The price range spans roughly **$410 to $478**.

The overall price action shows: a rally into late December (peaking around $476-478), a sharp decline into mid-January (~$418), a recovery rally to ~$462, then a significant bearish breakdown through February-March reaching lows around $412, followed by a tentative recovery attempt into early April around $456-460.

The chart is annotated with **12 numbered reference points** that correspond to the lesson text on the book page, each illustrating a specific price action principle.

Please make sure to read Part 1. We know from our analysis in the previous article that the market has a negative bias and that the conditions are extremely volatile for swing trades that last 3-4 weeks. We are only going to conduct price action analysis, but in future articles we will use all forms of technical analysis. The hollow candles in the chart are important since they have long bodies, short tails/wicks and relatively heavy volume. I will post the same chart many times so that the points are easier to reference. 13. The market is backing off from a recent high. These mixed candles are fairly long and this is a very wide range. It is a sign of indecision and volatility. A big move is likely. 14. A long red candle transitions us from one range to the next and it appears that sellers have the upper hand. However, we are still seeing giant mixed candles. We can favor the short side since the mid-point of the long red candle that transitioned us from one range to the next is still intact, but this is extreme volatility. Favor the short side, but keep it light. 15. Once again the market has gapped down and a new range has been established at a lower level. We are seeing tails under body and lots of mixed candles. That is a sign of weak trend strength and it is con�rmed by the light volume (blue line < 0). We can expect a bounce, so any short positions should be closed. It is way too early to go long. Since the beginning of the chart, the market has dropped 10%. We needed to use a swing trading tactic where we short bounces once they lose momentum and then we take gains and go to cash when we see signs of support. 16. The market bounced off of the low of the year and it �lled in a tiny gap. That bounce quickly found resistance and we know that from the compressed range and the mixed candles. The volume on this bounce was very light. The long red candle breached the compression (blue shaded area) on heavy volume. The mid-point held and this was a good area to enter swing shorts. 17. The market bounced off of a new low for the year on light volume and the mid-point of the red candle (16) has been preserved. The market did �ll in an earlier gap, but there is still one that has not been �lled. Buyers did not have the �re power to do so. The long green candle was immediately erased by a long red candle and sellers are still in control. We should expect follow through and we could test the low of the year. 18. Before the market could test the low of the year, buyers surfaced. The �rst candle is a doji and it does not present any problem. The next two candles are a bit more bullish. In both instances, the market opened below the prior close (gap down) and then the candle closed on the high of the day. The market also closed well above the low of the day and it is a sign that buyers are engaged. This could be a higher low double bottom that is forming and bearish swing traders should be taking gains on short positions. 19. The last two green candles have opened below the prior close and they have rallied during the day to close above the opening price. Support is starting to form and this looks like a higher low double bottom. Bearish swing traders should take remaining gains on short positions. It is way too early to get long. We need to have much more con�rmation before we consider that. 20. The market has been able to rally off of the low on light volume. The mid-point of the long green candle has been preserved. The market has been down 25% since the start of the year and that should keep us in a bearish mode. The bounce did not get very far and we are seeing a compression. 21. During this breakout we are seeing overlapping candles and that is a sign of weak trend strength. Each of these green candles started the day in negative territory. Sellers tested the bid early and buyers were able to power the market higher. This move feels like it is getting tired, but we do not have any technical con�rmation to short. 22. This is a nice gap down from the high. If the gap is preserved for a few days it will be a sign that buyers do not have enough power to �ll it and that will set up a good shorting opportunity. The last bar on this chart is signi�cantly lower than the �rst bar. The market has been very weak and this is o�cially a bear market (down more than 20%). A bearish opportunity could be setting up as we continue our price action analysis in the next article.

## 1. WHAT IS SHOWN

This is a **daily candlestick chart (D1)** of **SPY (S&P 500 ETF)**, spanning approximately from early April through mid-August. The chart includes a **volume panel** at the bottom (with raw volume bars in red/green and a 10-period volume moving average in blue). The price range covers roughly $365 to $455. The current price shown is approximately **$398.51**.

The overall price action tells a story of a **bear market decline**: the market starts near highs around $450, sells off significantly (down ~20%+), attempts multiple bounces, and by the end of the chart is showing weak recovery attempts. This is a comprehensive teaching chart that walks through **10 sequential price action lessons** (numbered 13 through 22), each illustrating a different tactical observation.

## 1. WHAT IS SHOWN

This is a **daily candlestick chart (D1)** of **SPY (S&P 500 ETF)**, spanning approximately from early April through mid-August. The chart includes a **volume panel** at the bottom (with raw volume bars in red/green and a 10-period volume moving average in blue). The price range covers roughly $365 to $455. The current price shown is approximately **$398.51**.

The overall price action tells a story of a **bear market decline**: the market starts near highs around $450, sells off significantly (down ~20%+), attempts multiple bounces, and by the end of the chart is showing weak recovery attempts. This is a comprehensive teaching chart that walks through **10 sequential price action lessons** (numbered 13 through 22), each illustrating a different tactical observation.

## 3. PATTERNS AND CONCEPTS BEING TAUGHT

This chart is a **sequential price action tutorial** that teaches traders how to read candles, volume, and market structure in real-time as a bear market unfolds. Each numbered point corresponds to a specific lesson from the article:

### **Point 13 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Indecision at Highs / Wide Range Mixed Candles**
**Rule: "When mixed candles are fairly long with very wide ranges at a high, it signals indecision and volatility. A big move is likely."**

The shaded zone shows candles with both long green and red bodies overlapping. Neither bulls nor bears have control. This is the calm before the storm ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ a massive sell-off follows.

### **Point 14 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Transition Between Ranges / Sellers Have Upper Hand**
**Rule: "When a long red candle transitions the market from one range to the next, sellers have the upper hand. Favor the short side since the mid-point of the transitioning candle remains intact, but keep it light because mixed candles mean extreme volatility."**

The shaded zone shows the market tried to consolidate at a lower level but the candles are still mixed (giant mixed candles). The mid-point of the long red candle that broke the market down hasn't been reclaimed ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ bearish.

### **Point 15 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Gap Down, New Range, Weak Trend Strength**
**Rule: "When the market gaps down and establishes a new lower level with tails under body and light volume (blue volume line < 0), it signals weak trend strength. Expect a bounce, but it's too early to go long."**

The market has dropped 10% from the top. The article recommends swing trading bounces ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ short bounces once they lose momentum, then go to cash at support. This is a **tactical bear market approach**.

### **Point 16 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Bounce into Resistance, Compression Zone**

The mid-point of the long red candle held and we saw continued selling. In the �rst candle with the blue arrow everything looks great. We had that �rst long red candle (23.) and then a doji below the low of that candle and then this long red candle. Everything is going great for a short position. However, notice how the next day the market gapped higher (solid red candle). Sellers regained control and the candle closed on its low, but there were some signs of buying. Also notice now the third candle with the arrow was red, but it had a massive gap up and then it spend the day drifting lower. It closed near its low, but buyers are interested. How do we know? If there were no interest on the part of buyers we would not have gapped higher. Orders to sell would have been layered above the close the previous day and there would not have been a gap up. Swing traders should take some gains here. A bounce looks likely. 25. The market staged a nice little rally and there were a few nice long green candles. The mid point of the long red candle (23) was preserved, but we did rally above the open from the long red candle (24). This long red candle (25) is very damaging for bulls. It erases the previous 3 long green candles and it closes on its low. We need con�rmation before we can re-enter shorts. The next candle is a doji at the low from the prior red candle and that is �ne. The next candle after that is red and it takes out the low from (24). This is a good entry point for shorts. The market gapped down to a new low of the year. The open of that candle was also the low for that candle and a massive gap reversal was underway and buyers were aggressive. By the close, this turned into a giant bullish engul�ng candle off of the low of the year. This is a sign of support. The next day a long red candle appeared, but the half-way point of the green engul�ng candle was preserved. The price action for the next few days stayed well above the mid-point of the long green candle and that is a sign of support. 29. The long green candle before the blue shaded area came on heavy volume and it closed above the open from a previous red candle (28). We are seeing long mixed green and red candles and that is a sign of volatility. The price action all year has been bearish. It is too early to consider longs, but we should expect volatility. 30. This long green candle came on heavy volume. It closed above the compression and the open from 3 prior long red candles. We are also seeing follow through buying. This is a time to wait on the sidelines. If the bounce stalls and we see tiny bodied candles and light volume, we can expect another wave of selling. If the rally continues on high volume, it might have room to run. Reading price action takes some time to learn, but how we get from point A to point B matters. How the current price action �ts into the longer term context also matters. These candles help us to gauge momentum. We can tell when it is building or waning. ## 3. PATTERN OR CONCEPT BEING TAUGHT

### **Concept: Distinguishing Real Breakouts from Fake Breakouts (Short-Covering Bounces)**

This chart illustrates the critical skill of **evaluating breakout authenticity** by looking at what happens AFTER the breakout rather than being seduced by the breakout itself.

### **The Setup:**
- SPY was in a **sustained downtrend** (bearish trend) with a clear downward-sloping trendline, price below major moving averages, and a series of lower lows/lower highs.
- On November 10, 2022, a "lighter than expected" CPI report triggered a massive rally that broke above:
  1. The downward-sloping trendline
  2. The 100-day moving average
  3. A horizontal resistance level (~$388-390)
- The breakout occurred on **heavy volume**

### **The Rules:**

**Rule 1 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Context Matters:**
"When a breakout occurs within a longer-term bearish trend, be skeptical ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ the move could be driven by short covering rather than genuine institutional buying."

**Rule 2 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ How to Confirm a Real Breakout:**
"When Asset Managers are buying aggressively, you will see:
- Small dips followed by quick recoveries
- Increasing volume on rallies
- The mid-point of the breakout candle may be tested, but it gets immediately bought up
- Follow-through buying within 2-3 days on good volume"

**Rule 3 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ How to Identify a Fake Breakout:**
"When the market cannot add to gains after a breakout, when volume dries up, and when there is no follow-through buying within 2-3 days, the breakout was likely a short-covering bounce ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ and traders/institutions will get MORE aggressive on the short side."

**Rule 4 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ The Behavioral Dynamic:**
"Short-term traders create breakouts through short covering but have no staying power. For a sustained move higher, you need long-term buyers (Asset Managers) to step in. Their absence is confirmed by lack of follow-through."

The most important lesson here is that **a breakout is not a signal ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ it is a question**. The breakout itself, no matter how dramatic, tells you very little. What matters is **what happens next**.

This can be used for stocks as well, but it is critical that you get your market bearings each day before you trade stock. Context is critically important when you are reading price action. What do the longer term daily charts look like? Is the market in a strong trend? Is the market trapped in a trading range longer term? Did we get to the current price with a Lamborghini or a bicycle? Are the candles mixed (weak trend) or are they of a single color (strong trend)? Is there overlap with other candles (weak trend) or are they stacked (strong trend)? All of these questions need to be answered so letÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂs start with a longer term chart of the SPY and then letÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂs drill down to an M15 chart and �nally an M5 chart. Reading price action is a skill that can be learned and it works. Below the charts you can read the scenarios I am expecting today with the probability of each. At the very bottom I conclude this section with a chart of what happened and a live video that I recorded on the opening bell where I described the price action bar-by-bar. Today the SPY is going to challenge a resistance level at $380 and it will open above it. Stacked green candles with little to no overlap in the �rst 30 minutes would be a sign of heavy buying. That scenario is unlikely because we know that sellers are present based on the recent price action. If we get that pattern the SPY will start to �ll in the D1 gap and we could have a few more days of follow through. There is no reason to chase anything in this market so I will be passive if this scenario plays out (20%). A gradual drift higher on the open with mixed overlapping candles would be a sign of weak trend strength. When that move stalls, a good shorting opportunity would set up. Look for a bearish hammer/bearish engulf off of the high of the day as a sign that a reversal is pending. This scenario has a 20% chance of playing out. A more likely scenario is a bid check. The market tries to �ll in some of the overnight gap up. Mixed overlapping candles will be a sign that the trend strength during the dip is weak. That will give us time to �nd stocks with relative strength and we can separate the fakes from the real deal. Once the market �nds support we can expect a rally and it will be time to buy these stocks. We do not want the retracement to be deep (more than half of the gap up preserved) or to last more than an hour. If that happens it would suggest decent selling pressure. This scenario has a good chance of playing out and it presents the best opportunities for us (30%). A strong gap reversal would have long red candles and brief pauses. Half of the overnight gains would easily be stripped away. This would suggest that sellers are fairly aggressive. The gap �ll would be fairly deep and the pullback will take a couple of hours to run its course. In this scenario you would focus on shorts. We want the bounces to last less than 30 minutes. This scenario has a 20% chance of playing out. The �nal scenario is a complete gap reversal. Stacked long red candles consecutively in the �rst 30 minutes with little to no overlap would be a sign of heavy selling. We have seen decent buying and the big down gap reversal two days ago tells us that buyers are aggressive enough to prevent that. This scenario only has a 10% chance of playing out. It is critically important to get the longer term context and then to drill down to the shorter time frames. Understand the possible scenarios and know the characteristics of each one. When they start to unfold, you will know what to expect and what action you plan to take. You should also know which scenario is most desirable and which one is most likely (they are not always the same). The chart below is how the day actually played out. The scenario we got was not the one we wanted. Gap and go patterns force us to chase early in the day and that is never wise. We do not have time to properly vet (observe) stocks and it is di�cult to separate the real from the fake. This pattern also has a tendency to run to its destination and compress. That makes it di�cult to trade the rest of the day. That means we have to trade smaller size early (because we donÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂt ever want to chase) so that we can make some money early in the day. It also means that we should take gains after 90 minutes of trading because the rest of the day the market will compress. Being able to read price action told us which scenario was going to play out and what actions we should take. The SPY stayed in that tight compression the rest of the day and there was a breakout in the last 10 minutes of trading. In the recording, you can clearly hear these predictions after 15 minutes of trading. IÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂm not clairvoyant, I just know how to read price action. > "When price is compressing within a range with extreme volatility and mixed overlapping candles, avoid swing trading. The whipsaws will stop you out. Day trading is more appropriate during these periods."

**Rule 5 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Volume Confirmation**:

4. **Take profits quickly** when bullish hammers appear at new lows ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ the breakdown move is ending
5. **Switch to day trading** during compression phases and during relief bounces after hammers appear

- Difficult to distinguish from fakes early in the day
- They force traders to chase, which is "never wise"
- The pattern tends to run to its destination and then compress
- It makes the rest of the day difficult to trade

**Rule 1 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Confirmation in 3 Bars:**

**Rule 2 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Time-Based Expectation:**
> "When a gap-and-go is confirmed, expect approximately one hour of upside movement, THEN expect the market to compress (trade in a tight range for the rest of the day)."

**Rule 3 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Trade Sizing for Gap-and-Go:**
> "When you identify a gap-and-go, trade smaller size early because you cannot easily separate the real move from the fake. Do not chase."

**Rule 4 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Post-Move Compression:**
> "When the initial gap-and-go move exhausts itself, expect tight compression. This compression makes it difficult to trade the rest of the day ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ accept this and reduce activity."

**Rule 5 ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Time Constraint:**
> "When trading a gap-and-go, take gains after 90 minutes of trading because the rest of the day the market will compress."

### What a trader should DO:
- Read the first 3 candles carefully to identify the pattern
- Trade smaller size because gap-and-go is hard to confirm vs. fakes
- Take profits within the first 60ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ90 minutes
- Once compression begins, **stop trading** or significantly reduce expectations
- Watch for a potential breakout in the last 10 minutes of the day (as mentioned in the book text)

### What a trader should AVOID:
- **Do NOT chase** the gap-and-go early in the day
- Do NOT continue trading aggressively once compression sets in

### The Deep Insight: **Pattern Recognition Within the First 15 Minutes Dictates the Entire Day**

Customize appearance Volume Reveals Conviction | OneOption - Stocks & Options Trading Suite Volume Reveals Conviction Market First 10 min read 2025-01-28 Heavy volume moves tell us that the move is legitimate and light volume tells us it canÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂt be trusted. Almost every technical indicator has two components: price and volume. That alone should tell you how important volume is to our technical analysis. Volume is very easy to analyze and it is either heavy, average or light. It does not require lengthy explanations so it does not get the attention it deserves. Consequently, it is overlooked by novice traders. LetÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂs not make the mistake of glossing over this topic. VOLUME CONVEYS VERY IMPORTANT INFORMATION AND IT NEEDS TO BE A MAJOR PART OF YOUR TECHNICAL ANALYSIS! I hope that got your attention. Volume tells us how excited buyers and sellers are. That in turn helps us gauge the strength of a trend. Our goal as traders is to predict price movement and sustained heavy volume helps us to determine direction. If a manufacturer reduced the price of their product there would be no way to measure the success/failure of the promotion without volume. They wouldnÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂt know if the product is moving or sitting on the shelves. Volume helps them determine the demand for it at that price and how much of it they need to produce. If the product is �ying off of the shelves and the line is out the door and around the corner, they can safely predict that this promotion will be successful. We canÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂt assess the quality of a market move without looking at volume. What if there is light volume and no move? This is common when the market is compressing in a tight range. It is a sign of equilibrium and neither side has an advantage. At some point a news item will spark a breakout one way or the other. Set alerts above and below the compression and wait. Since there is light volume, the trading range could last a long time. What if there is heavy volume and no move? This is a good scenario. The heavy volume indicates that buyers and sellers are interested. Shortly, one side or the other will prevail and that breakout is likely to have follow through (ÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂlegsÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ). On the breakout, the losing side will scramble to adjust and the winning side will add to positions. The breakout on volume will hit everyoneÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂs radar and the frenzy is on! Custom Search in Option Stalker Pro will �nd stocks with heavy volume that are in a compression. Set your alerts above and below the compression and wait for the breakout. Why do light volume rallies happen? We often see light volume rallies at the end of a long term uptrend. Because the trend is strong, sellers are extremely passive and they are holding out for a higher price. Even a small buyer can drive the price higher. Imagine this attitude on the part of the seller, ÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂIf you want it, come and get it at this nice high price. If you are not interested at that level, I will just hang on to it.ÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ This is what we call a sellers boycott. They are simply not interested in selling unless they get what they consider to be a premium. At that high price, buyers are not willing to load up so the volume remains light. A light volume spike to a new high could be a buying climax so pay attention to those because a drop is likely very soon. Of course, a light volume trend lower in a bear market would indicate that buyers are not interested. They are expecting lower prices and they will wait for signs of support. This is a ÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂbuyer boycottÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ and it can be characterized by this attitude, ÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂIf you are that anxious to sell, come and get me all the way down here.ÃÂÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂÃÂÃÂ Why do light volume bounces happen? - **Location**: A **blue arrow** pointing downward to a specific area in the indicator panel where both lines are hovering near or slightly below the zero line, during the ongoing green (bullish) zone on the right side of the chart.

It remains part of the **existing long bullish cycle**.

- The transition points between colors correspond to the crossover signals circled in the annotations.

- At the very bottom of the chart, there are small **volume bars** (teal/green colored), showing trading volume per period.

---

## 3. PATTERN OR CONCEPT BEING TAUGHT

This chart teaches **three critical concepts** about the 1OP indicator:

### Concept A: Sell Signal Generation
**Rule**: *"When the 1OP fast line (solid) crosses BELOW the slow line (dotted) after a spike upward, a SELL signal is generated."*

The trader should watch for the indicator to spike up (forming a peak), and then when the fast line rolls over and crosses below the slow line, this marks the beginning of a bearish cycle (pink zone). This is when a trader should consider short positions or exiting longs.

### Concept B: Buy Signal Generation
**Rule**: *"When the 1OP fast line (solid) crosses ABOVE the slow line (dotted) after a deep trough, a BUY signal is generated."*

The trader should watch for the indicator to plunge down (forming a deep trough), and then when the fast line turns up and crosses above the slow line, this marks the beginning of a bullish cycle (green zone). This is when a trader should consider long positions or exiting shorts.

### Concept C: The Zero Line Rule for Cycle Validation (MOST IMPORTANT)
**Rule**: *"When the indicator has not risen above zero during a bullish cycle and the lines begin to flatten or slightly cross near zero, do NOT consider this a new bearish cycle. The indicator must get above zero first before a subsequent bearish crossover can be considered a valid new bearish cycle."*

This is the nuanced rule being emphasized. Not every crossover is a valid signal. The indicator must complete a **full cycle** Ã¢ÂÂ meaning it needs to move meaningfully above zero during a bullish cycle before a bearish crossover carries weight. If it stays below or near zero, the bullish cycle is still considered intact.

---

## 4. MY UNDERSTANDING Ã¢ÂÂ CORE INSIGHTS

### The Deep Insight: Cycle Completion and the Zero Line as a Filter

The most important teaching on this chart is **Annotation 3** Ã¢ÂÂ the zero line filter. This is what separates a novice 1OP user from a skilled one. Here's why:

**The problem it solves**: In any dual-line crossover indicator system (similar in concept to MACD), there are frequent mini-crossovers, especially when momentum is weak or price is consolidating. A naive trader who acts on every crossover will get **whipsawed** Ã¢ÂÂ constantly entering and exiting positions during noise, accumulating losses.

**The solution**: The 1OP uses the zero line as a **cycle validation threshold**. A bullish cycle isn't "complete" until the indicator has risen above zero. Only after the indicator has been above zero can a subsequent bearish crossover be treated as a legitimate new bearish cycle. This prevents the trader from prematurely flipping to a bearish bias during what is actually a consolidation within an ongoing bullish move.

### Why This Setup is Valid
In this specific chart, the buy signal (Annotation 2) came from a **deep trough** Ã¢ÂÂ well below zero around -15 to -20. Deep troughs represent strong bearish momentum that has exhausted itself, making the subsequent bullish crossover a high-conviction signal. The text on the book page confirms: *"We like nice deep troughs, big spikes and defined crosses."*

The price then rallied significantly from ~$370.50 to ~$376.50, which is a substantial intraday move. During this rally, the indicator stayed near or below zero Ã¢ÂÂ it never made a meaningful spike above zero. This tells us the bullish momentum, while present in price, hasn't yet fully expressed itself in the indicator's cycle. Therefore, any downward crossover near zero is **premature** and should not be acted upon.

### What Would Make This Invalid (i.e., a True Bearish Signal)
If the indicator had:
1. Risen well **above zero** (creating a visible spike/peak above the zero line)
2. Then the fast line crossed below the slow line from that elevated position

...THEN it would be a valid bearish signal and the green zone would end. The key distinction is: **the cycle must complete (cross above zero) before the opposite signal can be trusted.**

### Connecting to the Broader Book Context
From the surrounding page text, this connects to the concept of **"benign" cycles** Ã¢ÂÂ when a cycle doesn't produce meaningful price movement, the next cycle in the opposite direction is more likely to produce. The text also emphasizes that when 1OP has many **mini crosses** near the zero line, the market trend strength is poor, price action is choppy, and the trader should **reduce trading activity**. The zero line proximity and lack of defined cycles is a warning to stay patient.

### Practical Trader Takeaway
- **Trade the deep troughs and big spikes** Ã¢ÂÂ these are high-conviction signals
- **Ignore crossovers near the zero line** that haven't completed a full cycle
- **The zero line is your filter** Ã¢ÂÂ it separates real cycle transitions from noise
- **When in doubt, stay with the current cycle** until the indicator proves otherwise by completing a full oscillation above/below zero
- This indicator is designed for **short-term/day trading** and should be combined with technical confirmation on longer-term analysis

### Concept: **Benign 1OP Cycles and Their Predictive Value**

This chart illustrates one of the most important nuances of using the 1OP indicator Ã¢ÂÂ the concept of **"benign" cycles** and how they set up expectations for the next cycle.

### The Rules:

**Rule 1 Ã¢ÂÂ Identifying Benign Cycles:**
*"When a 1OP cycle (bullish or bearish) does NOT produce a corresponding move in price, that cycle is considered 'benign.'"*

In this chart, the bullish cycle in the middle/right portion produced no meaningful upward price movement Ã¢ÂÂ price just chopped sideways. This is a benign bullish cycle.

**Rule 2 Ã¢ÂÂ Benign Cycles Increase the Odds of the Next Cycle Producing:**
*"When one cycle is benign (does not produce), the odds increase that the NEXT cycle in the opposite direction will produce a significant move."*

Since the bullish cycle was benign, the expectation is that the **next bearish crossover** should produce a meaningful downward move. The energy that wasn't released during the benign cycle effectively "loads the spring" for the next directional move.

**Rule 3 Ã¢ÂÂ Context Matters (Prior Trend Strength):**
*"When there was a big drop earlier in the day and a subsequent bullish cycle fails to produce, the bearish trend bias remains intact, and the next bearish cross is expected to produce."*

**Rule 4 Ã¢ÂÂ Failed Bearish Continuation as Range Signal:**
*"When a bearish cycle following a strong drop FAILS to produce a new low, it is a sign that the market might be trapped in a range."*

The first annotation explicitly teaches this Ã¢ÂÂ the second bearish cycle "should have" produced new lows given the momentum of the initial drop. When it didn't, that was a warning sign that a **range/consolidation** was forming rather than a continuation of the downtrend.

- **Recognize** when a cycle fails to produce Ã¢ÂÂ don't force trades during benign cycles
- **Anticipate** that the next opposing cycle has higher probability of producing
- **Monitor** whether bearish cycles after strong drops produce new lows Ã¢ÂÂ if not, expect range-bound action
- **Reduce position size** or **stay out** during obvious range-bound/benign periods
- **Wait for technical confirmation** before entering Ã¢ÂÂ don't blindly trade every crossover

- Trading every single 1OP crossover mechanically without reading context
- Going aggressively long during a benign bullish cycle in a bearish context
- Ignoring the failure of a bearish cycle to produce new lows (this is critical context information)
- Over-trading during choppy, range-bound conditions when the 1OP is hugging the zero line

The most profound lesson in this chart is that the **1OP indicator is not a mechanical system** Ã¢ÂÂ it is a **contextual framework**. The same crossover signal can mean very different things depending on:

The later crosses happened near zero and produced nothing. Crosses near zero with tight, intertwined lines indicate **poor trend strength** and likely range-bound conditions.

2. **Whether the prior cycle produced or not:** This is the "benign" concept, which is essentially a **momentum accounting system**. If a bullish cycle doesn't produce, it means buyers couldn't gain control Ã¢ÂÂ the path of least resistance remains down. This is analogous to how in physics, potential energy converts to kinetic energy. A benign cycle is stored potential energy.

3. **The broader context of the session:** The massive opening drop created a bearish bias. Every subsequent signal must be interpreted through that lens. A bullish cross in that environment has a much higher bar to clear than a bullish cross in a neutral or bullish context.

### What Makes This Setup Valid vs. Invalid:

**Valid benign cycle identification:**
- Clear prior directional move (the big drop) establishing context
- The subsequent cycle in the counter-trend direction (bullish) produces little to no price movement
- The indicator crosses occur near the zero line without deep peaks or troughs
- Volume is light during the benign cycle
- Price action shows mixed candles, tight ranges, dojis Ã¢ÂÂ indecision

**Invalid / Misidentification risks:**
- If the "benign" bullish cycle actually produced a modest rally but you dismissed it Ã¢ÂÂ you might be misreading the cycle

This chart teaches traders to think in **probabilities and sequences** rather than isolated signals. The **fundamental insight** here is that **the 1OP indicator's value is not just in its crosses, but in characterizing the QUALITY of each cycle to predict the NEXT cycle**. - The bearish cycle has mini crosses AND the price action confirms (small mixed candles, tight range)
- The indicator still achieved a "nice range" overall (deep trough before the bullish cross)
- The bullish cross occurs from a deep trough level (in this case around -27)
- Volume was low and unimpressive during the bearish cycle (confirming lack of conviction)

- If the bearish cycle had clean, deep crosses with good range AND price dropped significantly Ã¢ÂÂ that's a **productive** bearish cycle, not benign, and the next bullish cross might actually be the benign one
- If the indicator range was tiny (flat-lining near zero with mini crosses), even the next cycle may not produce Ã¢ÂÂ this would signal a **compression** where the indicator isn't providing useful information at all
- If the "benign" classification is applied too loosely Ã¢ÂÂ the text specifically notes "it is fairly uncommon for more than two cycles to be benign," meaning if multiple consecutive cycles are benign, the market condition is genuinely trendless and the indicator is unreliable

### The Nuance of "Nice Range":

1. **Benign cycle WITH nice indicator range** = "good sign" Ã¢ÂÂ next cycle likely produces (THIS CHART)
2. **Mini crosses with indicator tight to zero line** = poor trend strength, compression likely Ã¢ÂÂ minimize ALL trading

The difference is whether the indicator's envelope (peak to trough) was meaningful even though there were mini crosses within that envelope. In this chart, the 1OP went from a positive peak (circled upper left) all the way down to about -27 (circled at bottom) Ã¢ÂÂ that's substantial range. The mini crosses happened along the way but didn't prevent the overall move from peak to trough. This tells us the indicator is "working" and the next signal should be respected.

A skilled 1OP trader doesn't just trade crosses mechanically. They **build a running narrative of cycle quality**: "This bearish cycle is benign Ã¢ÂÂ lots of mini crosses, choppy candles, poor trend strength, but the indicator has good range. I'm going to stay patient and prepare for a potentially strong bullish cycle." This chart teaches **two critical concepts** about using the 1OP indicator:

### Concept A: Bullish Divergence as a Trend Strength Signal

**Rule: "When the market moves higher during a bearish 1OP cycle, this is a bullish divergence Ã¢ÂÂ it confirms the uptrend is strong and the next bullish cycle should produce significant gains."**

- The inverse is also true (from the page text): When the market drops during a bullish cycle, it's a bearish divergence suggesting the next bearish cross will produce well.
- Divergences are expected during **strong trends** and they **confirm trend strength** rather than contradict it.
- A trader should: Recognize that during a strong uptrend, bearish 1OP cycles that fail to push price lower are confirming signals to **trade from the long side** and expect the next bullish cycle to produce.

### Concept B: Mini Crosses Signal Weak/Unreliable Conditions

**Rule: "When 1OP has lots of small, tight crosses near the zero line (mini crosses), the trend strength is weak, the indicator is unreliable, and a trader should reduce position size or avoid trading the indicator signals."**

- The ideal 1OP pattern has **nice high spikes, deep troughs, and clean crosses** Ã¢ÂÂ this gives clean, tradeable signals.
- Mini crosses indicate: choppy/range-bound price action, tight ranges, low volume, mixed candles Ã¢ÂÂ a **compression** environment.
- A trader should: **Keep trading to a minimum** during mini-cross periods, not rely on the indicator, and recognize that a compression/breakout may be forthcoming.

### Concept C: Benign Cycles (from page context)

The page text also introduces the concept of **"benign" cycles** Ã¢ÂÂ when the market is flat during a bullish cycle, that cycle did not produce. A cycle that does not produce is called benign, and it increases the probability that the **next bearish cross will be a good one**. Each passing benign cycle that doesn't produce increases the odds that the next one will.

---

## 4. MY UNDERSTANDING Ã¢ÂÂ Core Insights

### The Deep Insight: 1OP Is a Trend-Confirmation Tool, Not a Reversal Signal

The fundamental nuance here is that **the 1OP indicator is most useful when the trend is strong, and it becomes unreliable when the trend is weak**. This is counterintuitive Ã¢ÂÂ many traders expect indicators to work in all conditions. The chart explicitly teaches traders to **recognize when the indicator's own behavior tells you not to trust it.**

### What Makes the Setup Valid vs. Invalid:

**VALID (High-Confidence Signals):**
- The 1OP oscillator makes **wide swings** with clear separation between peaks and troughs
- Crosses are **clean and definitive** Ã¢ÂÂ the fast line clearly crosses through the slow line
- **Divergences appear** Ã¢ÂÂ price moving against the cycle direction confirms the underlying trend is powerful
- The left side of this chart (JuneÃ¢ÂÂAugust) shows ideal conditions: deep troughs, high spikes, clean crosses, and a divergence that correctly predicted the massive July-August rally

**INVALID (Low-Confidence Signals):**
- The 1OP oscillator stays **flat and compressed** near the center line
- Numerous **mini crosses** occur in rapid succession
- The right side of this chart (SeptemberÃ¢ÂÂNovember) perfectly illustrates this: the market was choppy, volatile with mixed candles, and the 1OP produced numerous unreliable signals
- In this environment, taking every 1OP cross as a trade signal would result in whipsaws and losses

### The Practical Trading Framework:

1. **First, assess 1OP cycle quality** Ã¢ÂÂ Are the oscillator swings clean and pronounced, or choppy and compressed?
2. **If clean cycles:** Trade the crosses with confidence, look for divergences to confirm trend strength, and expect cycles to produce
3. **If mini crosses:** Step back, reduce size, wait for a compression breakout, rely on other forms of technical analysis
4. **Track benign cycles:** Each non-producing cycle loads the spring for the next one Ã¢ÂÂ consecutive benign cycles increase probability that the next cross will be significant
5. **Use technical confirmation:** The page emphasizes that 1OP signals require technical confirmation before taking trades Ã¢ÂÂ it's an early warning/preparation tool, not a standalone entry signal

### The Meta-Lesson:

The most sophisticated insight is that **the indicator tells you about itself**. When 1OP is working well (clean cycles, divergences), it's telling you the market has strong directional conviction and is tradeable. When it's producing mini crosses, it's telling you the market lacks directional conviction and you should wait. A skilled trader reads not just what the indicator says about the market, but what the indicator's behavior says about its own reliability in the current environment.

Customize appearance Solving Today's Puzzle | OneOption - Stocks & Options Trading Suite The �rst hour of trading sets the tone. The price action in recent days will provide us with context and weâll know if buyers or sellers have control and to what degree. Before the opening bell, the overnight action will give us an indication of where the market is going to open and weâll compare that price to the previous dayâs open, high, low and close. If the market is going to open outside of that range, we will zoom out to see if any other signi�cant price levels are in range. Many trading sessions feature mixed overlapping candles on light volume and the price action is âprogram drivenâ. There are days when we should not trade /ES and we are going to avoid these sessions because our odds are low. Instead, we are going to focus on moves where we have nice tight orderly price action with candles of a single color on heavy volume. When we have that pattern, we know that one side (buyers or sellers) is motivated and we will reference the previous dayâs candle to structure our trades. Take breaks as needed and draw relationships between todayâs price action and yesterdayâs price action. It will help you understand if the recent trend is going to continue or reverse and your conclusions will help you plan for tomorrow. Challenge yourself to visualize whatâs happening. On the left side of the chart below you will see a normal D1 bullish candle. It has a tail and a wick and the close was higher than the open so it is green. The previous D1 candles were red and they were higher up. This candle closed in the prior dayâs range and it could be a sign of support. Was this green candle a âone offâ and now the decline will resume? If that scenario is true, what type of M5 candles would we want to see today? The �rst hour of trading is going to provide us with important clues on how to trade during the day and the overlays are M5 bars during the �rst hour. Horizontal mixed overlapping candles are not going to provide us with any information. We are not going to try to predict the �ight of a bat so we are not going to consider days that have that pattern. We are only going to consider orderly stacked candles of a single color that have good volume in our examples. Those are signs of aggression and our odds of predicting future price movement are high. When you take a look at the chart you will notice lines for the open, high, low close and midpoint. All of the scenarios would be bearish since the trend has been bearish and since we are seeing stacked red candles. Before the trading session starts, weâll know where in the prior dayâs range the market will open. The SPY closed at the green dotted line so the �rst scenario on the left would be very bearish. That is a big gap down below the prior low. There is likely some overnight news to spark selling of this magnitude so check the news wires. The issue with Gap and Go (gap down and continue) formations like this is that we have a fair amount of risk early in the day. If the market reverses into the gap, it has plenty of room to travel higher. Those reversals happen quickly and they lead to large losses. We will cover this in great deal later in the course. As the drift lower unfolds you would start small and add on con�rmation. Whatâs con�rmation? We want to see future candles that have very little retracement into the previous candle. We also want lower highs and lower lows. We also want to see mostly red candles. This type of price action tells us that sellers are aggressive. They are keeping the pressure on and they are hitting bids. When we get this pattern, the risk of a gap reversal decreases after the �rst hour. In the second overlay, the �rst red candle starts at the open from the prior day (red dotted line). This is a reasonable gap down. Since it is in the prior dayâs range, we want to attack that previous low of the day early and we want to take it out convincingly with consecutive reds. This scenario gives us better odds because there is not a big drop overnight and we are not chasing. The third overlay is even better. The market opens close to where it closed the prior day. We see nice reds and the mid-point is taken out. The trend has been lower in recent days so we are anxious to take shorts. When we see the mid-point breached easily, we can take a starter short. When it takes out the open from the prior day, with ease, we can add to the position. When it easily challenges the prior dayâs low we can add to the position. The price action is telling us that sellers are aggressive. That little D1 bounce the day before is providing sellers with a great opportunity to add to shorts. The �nal overlay is a gap up and I love this pattern. The D1 green candle from the prior day might be attracting some dip buyers. That gap up is instantly smacked down. When we have early red candles right away, the market is in the overnight gap and we can take a starter short. This is a nice entry point and we are joining the recent down trend. We add on follow through into the gap when the midpoint of the gap fails (open today â prior close/2). We add when the prior dayâs high fails and we add when the gap �lls (prior close). This move has the potential to erase the entire previous day and the momentum will build. This is a classic example of why it is more dangerous to buy a Gap and Go up than it is to look for a Gap Reversal. Most days the market has a gaps and we are going to cover them in great detail. For now, just focus on the recent price action, the previous day and the current day. My �rst objective is to get you to think about how todayâs puzzle piece �ts into the whole. This is important. Close your eyes and clear your head. In the example below the green candle is a new relative high and the market has been in a steady trend higher. When a trend is in place, you donât ever know when it is going to pause or reverse. When we get an indication of where the market will open today, we put that move into the longer-term context and into the context of the prior dayâs range. We donât know if the �rst hour will be bullish or bearish, but we know that we want to see nice a nice orderly M5 trend featuring candles of a single color. That tells us that one side is aggressive. In the �rst overlay below, the market opened way below the prior days low. This was a big gap down and a move of this magnitude would likely result from a news release. Check the news to determine what spooked the market. Could this be a longer-term concern? Since the market has been in a recent up trend, there is plenty of downside room and a Gap and Go lower is possible. That move would �ush out bullish speculators and it has a chance to gather steam. We donât like to chase Gap and Go moves so take small starter positions if the red candles start to stack. Only add if the move is orderly with little to no retracement. Since the market has been in an uptrend it will be well above the moving averages. You will have to reference previous long green candles to determine where to add to short positions. The mid- points, opens and lows from those candles will provide support and you want to see them obliterated. In the second overlay, the gap was not as severe. It is not uncommon to see the previous dayâs gains wiped out, but you should check the news to see if something has changed. The market is still in the prior dayâs range and weâll see if the selling pressure is heavy enough to take out the low of the day. We want that level attacked in the �rst hour and we want to breach it easily. If that level holds, it will be a sign that buyers are still interested. If we see stacked red candles and heavy volume we would take a position when the market gets through the prior dayâs low and we would add on follow through similar to what we did in the �rst example. In the third overlay below, the market opens where it closed the previous day. This is a �at open and we are watching for movement in either direction. The market quickly tests the mid-point. We are very cautious shorting in a D1 up trend and we are mentally in a camp where we want support levels to hold. We want to buy dips and we prefer to trade from the long side (bullish). As the action unfolds, we see decent volume and now we are testing the open from the prior day. If the selling pressure has been steady and tight, we might take a small starter short position. Our stop would be a rally above the mid-point. We want to immediately test the low from the prior day and we want to blow through it. We need that speed because it indicates urgency on the part of sellers. We also need heavy volume or the price action could just be âsell programsâ pushing the market around. If we get that new low for the day, we can add to the short position. If the market continues to drift lower all day, we should consider reducing some of our short-term bullish swing trades. In the �nal overlay, the market gaps up to a new relative high. It is above the prior high. Gap reversals off of a new relative high are fairly common because they attract pro�t taking. If you look at a D1 chart, �nd the peaks and look for long red candles. Before you get too excited, let me splash a little cold water on this. If you look at the longer-term up trend before the peak, you will notice lots of gaps higher. Those candles �nished green and the close was higher than the open. Each of them signaled that buyers were aggressive. Just because we have a gap up to a new relative high does not mean that we are going to see a nasty reversal. We need to see stacked red M5 candles early! They will instantly send the market back into the gap. Mixed overlapping candles into the gap is NOT what we want. Those are mildly bullish and the drift lower is simply con�rming support. A move of this nature will �nd support and buyers will fuel a move back to the high of the day and beyond. I canât say this strongly enough, for a gap reversal, these need to be stacked, red and relentless like we see in the overlay below. When we see a gap reversal off of a relative high, sellers are not taking any prisoners and they are going to smash every bid. This is one of my favorite trading patterns. If the �rst candle is long and red, I would take a starter short in the �rst few bars if the volume is heavy. Next we want the market to attack the mid-point of the gap. If it does, you would add there. The next support level is the prior dayâs high. If that fails, we add. Next we have the prior dayâs close. That will typically be support. The gap has �lled and the trade might have run its course. If the market �nds support there, you should take gains. If this is how the day concludes, it was just the �rst sign of resistance. Nothing to worry about. Just watch for future selling at this level. If the market tries to advance and it canât, the upward momentum will stall here. If the market continues to leak lower, the mid-point of the candle is the next support, then the prior dayâs open and then the prior dayâs low. If you get this pattern, a giant bearish engul�ng candle will form on a daily chart (D1). That has long-term implications. I would exit short-term bullish swings and I would be ready to pare back on longer-term swings. This is a meaningful high for at least a month. Letâs take a little break. The chart below and the chart above are identical. What changed? The context. In the �rst instance the green candle appeared after a down trend. Sellers were in control and we were trying to determine if that green candle was a �uke or if it was a sign of support. Given the M5 pattern, it con�rmed that sellers were still aggressive because the candles were red and stacked. We would expect more selling ahead. In the second case, the green candle appeared when the market was trending higher. During an up trend, we are going to look for signs of resistance. We donât want to short in an up trend and it would take some orderly stacked red candles on heavy volume to demonstrate that sellers are in control. Depending on the opening price, we had different perspectives and day trading approaches. Next letâs take a look at the â�ip sideâ. We will go through this exercise once more, but this time with stacked green candles. Repetition is good if you are learning how to read price action. It is a mental exercise and you need to be able to visualize whatâs happening without studying a bunch of charts and patterns. This is like a professional Black Jack player learning to count cards. In the chart below the ânormalâ green candle appeared after a series of red candles and the market had been trending lower. Was that green candle a âone offâ or could support be forming? What type of price action would tell us that buyers were interested? Take a look at the chart. In the �rst overlay, the market opened well below the low from the prior day. This was a big overnight gap down and given where the market was going to open you should check to see if there was major news. The recent trend was down and this could have been sellers taking advantage of the bounce the previous day. On that gap down, buyers instantly supported the market. The stacked green candles moved instantly into the gap and the volume was heavy. You could take a small starter long on the notion that this could be a gap reversal off of a relative low (another favorite pattern of mine). We had seen some buying the previous day. As it quickly recovered the mid-point of the gap (prior dayâs close â open today/2) it was apparent that buyers were interested and we could add to our long. If the rally maintains the momentum we want to move quickly above the prior dayâs low. This is where we would expect to see some resistance. If there have not been any dips, hold on to your position. It is alright for the market to pause, but we want the move to continue in the next few bars. The market has recently been in a down trend and we know that buyers are always interested given the 100-year bullish trend. If this move continues you can add at the lines when we enter the body of the D1 candle. If the market takes out the high from the previous day it is going to result in a giant green engul�ng candle D1. That will be a major turning point and at minimum this gap reversal off of a relative low will be a short-term low that will last at least a month. We should expect follow through buying the next few days. Exit longer-term bearish swings and short- term bearish swings. Also consider taking some short-term bullish swing trades. In the second overlay below, the market gapped lower, but it found support just above the prior dayâs low. The market had been in a down trend so sellers were just probing for support. We would want to see an instant âpopâ right from the open to tell us that the prior day was not a �uke. Buyers were interested at that level the day before and they are still there. The steady price action and stacked greens on volume tell us they are eager to buy more at that level. You can add to day trades on at all of the lines. In the third overlay, the market tests the mid-point of the long green candle and it jumps off of it. This small overnight drop was just a small round of pro�t taking after a green candle in a down trend. When the market moved higher quickly, it was a sign that buyers were interested. We would add at the prior close and at the prior dayâs high. The �nal overlay below is bullish. The market gaps up the next day. We have to tread cautiously at �rst. We can take a very small starter long and we need to make sure that this is not a gap up to lure in bullish speculators. That head fake would get quickly hammered down. After a few bars, we know the move is legitimate and we can add to the position. The recent down trend leaves plenty of upside and longer-term buyers are going to view this as a good entry point now that support has been established and con�rmed. From this point on, you will have to reference previous long red candles. We want the market to easily move above the open from those candles. All of the M5 patterns below are bullish. It was more a matter of con�rming that buyers were genuinely interested after a recent trend lower. This low is going to set up a nice entry point for longs and we should expect it to continue. You would exit long-term and short-term bearish swing trades. Remember, we are always on âthin iceâ when we are shorting. This would also be a time to take some short-term bullish swing trades and perhaps some longer-term bullish swing trades. Scale in. We need to make sure that this bounce is legitimate. This is the same chart as above, but the market has been in an uptrend. You are probably getting pretty good at this by now so letâs speak in general terms. The last green candle formed a new relative high. If we come in the next morning and we see a gap down, we should instantly be checking the news wires. That was a pretty good smack down. The SPY closed on its high the prior day and this gap down is way below the prior day low. In an up trend, pro�t taking is usually not going to be the reason for a move like this. There was some news that âspookedâ the market. It might not have been a cause for concern and one of our best set-ups is to buy a gap down. That provides us with an excellent entry point to join the longer-term up trend. Once the move unfolds we can see that buyers are interested and the market gets right into the gap and into the prior dayâs range. The two middle candles are both nice overnight dips into the prior dayâs range with strong recoveries and both provided nice buying opportunities. We can add to long positions as we get through various price levels. The last overlay we have to be a little more cautious with. We know that gaps up to a new relative high often result in gap reversals and they attract pro�t taking. Be particularly careful buying Gap and Go patterns if the market has been strong in recent days. Once we see the �rst few candles we can take a small starter long. We can add on con�rmation. We are going to move through these next charts quickly. Letâs say that the red candle below is part of a recent down trend. The �rst overlay is a gap reversal off of a relative low. We want the market to scream higher from that low and to spark massive short covering. We want the market to run hard through all of the price points from the red D1 candle and if it can do that, a giant green engul�ng candle will result on the D1 chart. Take gains on short-term and long-term shorts and consider taking some long-term bullish swing trades. This is a major turning point. The two middle scenarios are more reasonable moves and they are inside of the prior dayâs range. Both will result in nice bullish day trades. At this juncture, it is just one good day in a market down trend. They could signal support, but we need to tread very cautiously before we reach that conclusion. The market would have to continue higher during the day on massive volume, it would need to close on itâs high of the day and well above the prior dayâs close. The last overlay we have to be careful with because that is massive gap up in a down trend. Something has changed overnight and we need to tread cautiously to make sure the move is legitimate. We do not want to get trapped in a gap reversal since the market is still in a down trend. If the move continues higher the rest of the day, this could signal that support is forming. Letâs say that long red D1 candle below appears during a bullish trend. This gap down was not that dramatic because the previous day the market closed near its low. On the open, buyers jumped on that opportunity. Bearish speculators got too excited and they are going to get the door slammed in their face. Picking market tops is a losing proposition and they are going to get squeezed. The two middle overlays are nice set ups. The market gaps up and it quickly moves through the price levels. There were many opportunities to get long and to add. The brief dip in the up trend was quickly resolved. The �nal overlay is a massive gap up. We saw selling the prior day and we know gaps up to a new relative high often result in a gap reversal. Check the news and gradually scale in. You need to tread cautiously. This is not a pattern you want to get aggressive with because a gap reversal would be costly. Start slow and add. If the pattern is tight and orderly and the volume is heavy, it is a sign that buyers are aggressive. The next two D1 charts below are dojis. The bodies are small and the wicks and the tails are long. If the volume was heavy during these days, it indicates that buyers and sellers are active. There are going to be head fakes while both sides battle it out. In the �rst chart below the market opens near the prior high and it reverses. Make sure that when the prior day high is breached, the candles are stacked and green. The volume needs to be heavy and you want to take out that high early in the day. When we break through the prior day low, we want to do it early in the day and on heavy volume. We need those stacked red candles. If the candles are mixed and they are scattered the prior dayâs range, the market is not ready and there is no clear direction. In the charts below I featured two long candles. The red one is closing on its low of the day and there is no tail (a small tail is �ne). This is a sign of heavy selling right into the close. We want those long candles preserved. After a big move down, the SPY will usually take a break the next day and it will be an âinside dayâ. It is fairly uncommon to see big days back-to-back and you will notice this if you look at a D1 chart. Ideally, the mid-point from the long red candle is preserved. The candle the next day can be green or red. They are usually pretty small. Often there will be a small bounce and that is why I colored it green. Two or three days after that long red candle you should watch for follow through selling and that is the M5 pattern you want. Stacked red candles on volume through the low from that red candle will signal that sellers are back. The SPY was not able to rally above the mid-point so sellers were never far away. In the chart on the right we have a giant green candle that closed on the high of the day (no wick). There can be a small wick, we just want to see that relentless buying right into the close. The next day will be an âinside dayâ and we want half of the long green candle preserved. There will often be a little pro�t taking and that is why I colored it red. Two or three days after that long green candle we will see follow through buying and we want to see those stacked green candles on volume blow through the high from the long green candle. That is a sign that buyers are back. One �nal note. If the intraday move is very steep (60 degrees or more), it is not sustainable. When you see long candles that are erased (at the high or low), take gains. Sharp moves like this will often produce a large contra move. The strength of the �rst move is legitimate, the contra move is not. Wait for the contra move to stall and you will get âanother bite from the appleâ. If the initial intraday move has a very gradual slope, you will have opportunities to build a position, add to it and ride it. On the left side of the chart below you will see a sharp initial drop. This is going to produce a tall bounce and you need to take gains when the long red candle at the low of the day is erased by two green candles. When that move stalled, there was an opportunity to short on the rejection from VWAP (it is anchored to the �rst trade of the day). On the right side of the screen shot below you can see that a nice gradual drift lower is forming and how the SPY was not able to get above VWAP . When that resistance held, we were able to add to the trade and we also had an opportunity to add at the prior dayâs low. The recent trend and the prior dayâs candle provide us with important information about what we should expect today. We conduct pre-open research and we determine where the market is likely to open based on the overnight session. If the open is projected to be outside of the previous dayâs range, we identify other key price levels that might be in play. If it is fairly tight to the prior days range (or inside of it) we use the open, high, low, close and midpoint to guide us. We know the bullish and bearish M5 patterns to watch for and we formulate a game plan. As this nice, tight orderly patterns are forming, we scale in. We donât trade mixed overlapping candles on light volume particularly if the market is going to open inside of the prior dayâs range. The price action today is going to provide us with valuable information when we set up our game plan tomorrow. The context in this lesson was very short- term in nature. This is where it gets exciting. We are going to zoom out in the next lesson and you are going to be able to visualize what the intraday M5 price action probably looked just by looking at a longer-term D1 chart.
